original_classification_or_claim: Reported contradiction rates in degraded configurations (6-lead: 7.8%, 2-lead: 18.9%, 1-lead: 22.7%) represented physiological contradictions.
corrected_interpretation: The existing classifier conflated unavailable sensor leads with physiological contradictions. When genuine physiological contradictions (HR bounds) are separated from unmeasured leads, the true contradiction rate is flat across all configurations (~1.0%-1.5%: 12-lead: 1.14%, 10-lead: 1.00%, 8-lead: 1.03%, 6-lead: 1.17%, 4-lead: 1.17%, 2-lead: 1.22%, 1-lead: 1.46%). Reported aggregate rates reflect channel-loss reclassification and are unsuitable for clinical contradiction assessment.
remaining_limitation: Re-classifying all 25,816 individual trace dossiers into separate 'Required evidence unavailable' vs 'Physiologically contradictory' JSON fields requires a separately approved future pipeline run without modifying frozen weights.

original_classification_or_claim: In 6-lead, 'anterior myocardial infarction or conduction disturbance' claims drove 289 contradictions due to attention querying masked precordial leads.
corrected_interpretation: Retracted. Audited validation traces show exactly 0 cases of anterior MI among the 289 contradictions. All 246 channel-unavailability cases were conduction blocks: 130 RBBB and 116 LBBB. The remaining 43 cases were physiological HR contradictions (39 STACH, 4 SBRAD). 6-lead MI predictions (668 traces) were all classified as 'Insufficient evidence to assess' because limb leads satisfied the contiguous-pair check.
remaining_limitation: Candidate disease acronym space contains only generic 'MI' without anatomical anterior subclassing.

original_classification_or_claim: Preservation of V1 in 4-lead provides anatomical grounding that explains both the contradiction rate drop (from 289 to 43) and superior 4-lead AUROC over 6-lead.
corrected_interpretation: Retracted. The physiological contradiction count was identical between 6-lead and 4-lead (43 vs. 43). The apparent reduction from 289 to 43 was an artifact of line 108: in 4-lead, V1 is present in the lead mask, so RBBB (144) and LBBB (126) were reclassified into 'Insufficient evidence to assess' rather than 'Contradictory'. Zero traces gained verified clinical grounding. The causal link between V1 retention and AUROC superiority remains an untested hypothesis.
remaining_limitation: AUROC differences derive from representation learning in Module 3 latents, not post-hoc trace generator heuristics.

original_classification_or_claim: Trace consistency classifications represent a uniform evaluation of all eight target disease categories.
corrected_interpretation: Retracted. The existing classifier applies selective lead-feasibility rules to RBBB, LBBB, and MI (shunting them to 'Contradictory' when leads are missing), while completely omitting lead checks and contradiction checks for NORM, AFIB, and 1AVB (which remain 'Insufficient'). Furthermore, attention querying masked leads is silently absorbed into 'Insufficient' for NORM/AFIB/1AVB, whereas it demotes SBRAD/STACH from 'Consistent'.
remaining_limitation: Comprehensive contradiction rules covering QRS morphology, PR interval prolongation, and rhythm irregularity remain unimplemented in Module 4 v3.
